verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 3 advisories. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. The second-registry finding is fully repaired and the delta is complete at 20-for-20; the SHOULD-FIX is that the one new digest citation v9 introduces does not resolve against live bytes, and v9 carries no v9-authoring custody record in which that strand could be recorded.

shouldFix.title: The fixture-corpus v2 digest citation does not resolve against live bytes, and v9 adds no reMeasurementAtV9 in which the strand could be recorded
detail: whatThisDoesNotDo[1] now cites component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v2.json at e2781f449599909c7b2bfc8d827591911323f8633e2b5f419fcb27e772e6c9da. I re-measured that file: its live sha256 is 70248781118452308399e91fcbecb7cac37dd5d58fd03c49ac9efcec445341d5. The citation does not resolve.

The cause is a mutual pin. Corpus v2's schemaContract now reads {path: docs/coop/artifacts/component-manifest-schemas.v9.json, sha256: 52b3ab93d531d7e229f098deef8d944040bc93461c3e5c70be775002a6f7b791, standing: UNDER-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW} - it pins THIS subject. When I measured v2 during the v8 round it pinned v8 at 22c9fbad..., so v2 was edited to re-point at v9 after v9 was frozen, and that edit is what moved its digest. I record explicitly that v9's citation was almost certainly accurate at v9 authoring; it stranded afterwards.

That makes the strand structural rather than accidental: any digest v9 carries for a file whose own contents pin v9 is invalidated by the very act of that file adopting v9. A bare digest cannot stay valid across that cycle.

v9 neither anticipates the cycle nor records it. /sources is byte-identical to v8 in its entirety - there is no reMeasurementAtV9. That breaks a practice the chain established under a blocker: Codex's V7-B1 required that a new authoring-custody key get 'its own named ADD operation', and v6, v7 and v8 each carried reMeasurementAtV6 / AtV7 / AtV8 recording that successor's predecessor digest and its live-pin state. v9 carries none, so there is no place where the corpus-v2 live pin, or the fact that the cited pin has stranded, could be written down.

The three other new citations in the same sentence all resolve exactly: corpus v1 at d81a4ef9ed26405a07e84ae0be9a3d2048fd9a6126b1f93d139a5a499204b542, and its two REJECT verdicts at 2bbdc392e8167809a0ec0a14a2058dc99b78c9e4ef947ad125cc1b8ad604e03f and 4509ee425c34c84a6af22230a1de7dea9779704ea7af2bfc1b3be50b24644d20. Both of those verdict files do carry verdict REJECT, so the disposition claim is accurate. The defect is confined to the v2 pin.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Applying the artifact's own citationDiscipline - 'whole-document pins strand on any edit of the cited file. Independent review re-verifies the named property if a digest has moved' - I re-verified every named property of the v2 citation and all hold: the file exists, its reviewStatus is still DRAFT-AWAITING-SCHEMA-SUCCESSOR exactly as cited, and 'draft against this schema lineage' is now true in the strongest sense since it pins v9 itself. Nothing asserted about the design is false, and the non-acceptance boundary is intact.
shouldFix.whyItIsStillSHOULDFIX: The repair recorded as REPAIRED under both V8-A3 and CODEX-V8-S1 was specifically to pin corpus v2 at a digest, and the pin as delivered is unresolvable. A reviewer following it gets a mismatch and must reconstruct why. The artifact has both a policy for stranded pins and a mechanism for recording live ones, and v9 used neither for the single new pin it introduced.
shouldFix.remedy: Either cite corpus v2 by path plus named properties with the mutual-pin cycle stated (so no digest is promised that cannot hold), or add /sources/reMeasurementAtV9 by a named ADD operation recording the v9-authoring live pin for corpus v2 alongside the predecessor digest, on the reMeasurementAtV8 pattern. The second option also restores the per-successor custody practice.

repairVerification.finding: V8-S1 (Claude SHOULD-FIX) and V8-A1 (Codex advisory) - the V7-A2 repair added a second open-decision registry beside /namedOpenDecisions
repairVerification.howIChecked: /openDecisions is removed, and it is the only top-level key change in either direction - v9's top-level key set is otherwise identical to v8's. OD-2 now lives in /namedOpenDecisions, whose ids read [OD-1, OD-2], so the id convention is restored. I compared the entry shapes directly: OD-1 has {id, decision, standing, candidateOwners, consequence} and OD-2 has the same five plus priorId, so it adopts the container's convention rather than importing the old one. The priorId 'OD-V8-1' is a useful provenance breadcrumb, and OD-2's standing sentence states the move in the open: 'Previously recorded at v8 /openDecisions[OD-V8-1]; moved here so this surface's open decisions are one lookup.' /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor is updated to point at 'namedOpenDecisions OD-2'. Enumerating this surface's open decisions is now a single lookup, which is exactly what my finding asked for. Codex's V8-A1 is the same issue at advisory grade and is answered by the same repair.
repairVerification.residual: See advisory V9-A3 on the register-side consequence.

Corpus v1 matches at d81a4ef9...; the claude2 v1 verdict matches at 2bbdc392...; the codex v1 verdict matches at 4509ee42...; and I confirmed both of those files carry verdict REJECT, so 'independent REJECT verdicts' is accurate and correctly attached to the verdict files rather than to the candidate digest - which was precisely Codex's point. repairVerification.note: Both reviewers' findings converged on this sentence and v9 folds them as two separate entries rather than merging, which keeps each reviewer's finding traceable. That is good practice and I record it as such.

repairVerification.finding: V8-A1 and V8-A2 (Claude advisories) - redundant appended clauses on historical reMeasurement notes, and the 'now accounted by' non-sequitur
repairVerification.howIChecked: v9 does not claim these were repaired. /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor states 'V8-A1 and V8-A2 are carried: no further mutation of historical reMeasurementAtV2/V5 notes; no claim that adding reMeasurementAtV8 accounts for v7's unnamed reMeasurementAtV7.' I verified both undertakings hold on the bytes: /sources is byte-identical to v8 in its entirety, so neither historical note was touched again, and no new repairLog entry repeats the accounting claim I objected to. Neither advisory appears in the method roster or as a repairLog entry. As their author I confirm both were advisory-grade and neither was required to meet the ACCEPT bar.

advisories.title: citationDiscipline is still written in v6's voice and is three successors stale
advisories.detail: The field reads 'Whole-document digests in bindingSources are v2-authoring measurements (measuredAtV2Authoring), NOT V6-AUTHORING CLAIMS ... Live pins at v6 are recorded only at reMeasurementAtV6.' It is byte-identical since v6, but the document now also carries reMeasurementAtV7 and reMeasurementAtV8. Read as historical scoping - the live pins as of v6 are at reMeasurementAtV6 - the sentence is true. Read as the artifact's standing rule for where live pins live, it is false, since v7 and v8 each recorded their own. Given that V9-S1 turns on exactly this question - where a v9-authoring live pin would go - the field is the natural place to state the rule once in version-neutral terms: 'live pins at authoring N are recorded at reMeasurementAtVN'.
advisories.notBlocking: Ambiguous rather than false, and no measurement depends on it.

advisories.title: The basedOn.method roster lists the four entries in a different order than the repairLog appends them
advisories.detail: The method names 'V8-S1, CODEX-V8-S1, V8-A3, META-v9'; the repairLog appends V8-S1, V8-A3, CODEX-V8-S1, META-v9. The sets are identical, and the method's claim is set membership - every path not named by one of these entries is unchanged - so nothing about the completeness guarantee is weakened, and I verified that guarantee holds. Noting it only because v6, v7 and v8 each matched in order, and a reviewer comparing the two lists mechanically will see a mismatch before working out that it is immaterial.
advisories.notBlocking: Cosmetic; the completeness property is unaffected and verified.

advisories.title: Applying v9 will require the register's DR-103 row to name OD-2, and v9 does not name that obligation
advisories.detail: The live SRC-08 DR-103 row enumerates this surface's open decisions as 'named open decision OD-1 ... remains OPEN with its owner UNASSIGNED between DR-115 and DR-120'. v9 adds OD-2 to the same container, correctly and at my request. The consequence is that on application the row will under-report this surface's open decisions unless it is amended to name OD-2 as well. v9 records no such reconciliation obligation. This is coordinator-facing rather than a defect in the schema - the artifact binds NOTHING and reconciliation belongs to the application act - but it is the kind of downstream obligation this artifact elsewhere names explicitly, and I flag it here rather than touching file 08, which I did not edit.
advisories.notBlocking: OD-2 is correctly recorded on this surface; only the register-side echo is outstanding, and only at application time.

attackListDisposition.detail: /openDecisions is gone; it is the only top-level key removed and no key was added. OD-2 sits in /namedOpenDecisions in that container's own shape and id convention, with a priorId breadcrumb to OD-V8-1. One registry, one lookup.

All four claims are now digest-cited, which is a real improvement over v8's single pin - and the REJECT disposition is now correctly attached to the two verdict files rather than to the candidate digest. Three of the four digests re-measure exact. The corpus-v2 pin does not resolve; see V9-S1.

Those subtrees carry the no-lock-until-DR-111 statements at lockSchema.purpose, resolutionInputs.type, resolutionInputs.semantics and ID-DEP-4, the DR-111 gate on every lock-bearing corpus member, and RJ-4's INACTIVE lock-digest arm. V8-S1 covers the REMOVE of /openDecisions, the ADD of /namedOpenDecisions[OD-2], and /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor[0]. V8-A3 and CODEX-V8-S1 both cover /whatThisDoesNotDo/1. No creep at any of the 20 diff sites.

attackListDisposition.attack: Inventing findings the named v8 verdicts do not contain
attackListDisposition.detail: I read both v8 verdicts and enumerated their ids. Claude 2 v8: REJECT, blockers [], shouldFix [V8-S1], advisories [V8-A1, V8-A2, V8-A3] - v9's claude2V8 record states precisely that, and I confirm as its author. Codex v8: REJECT, blockers [], shouldFix [V8-S1], advisories [V8-A1] - v9's codexV8 record states precisely that. The idCollisionNote is accurate on all three counts: Codex V8-S1 is the fixture-citation SHOULD-FIX, my V8-S1 is the second-registry SHOULD-FIX, and Codex V8-A1 is the same second-registry issue at advisory grade - I verified each against the source verdict text. Every repairLog entry corresponds to a finding present in a named verdict file, and no v8 finding is left unaddressed or misattributed.

whatIVerified.digestIntegrity: Subject measured with python3 hashlib at start and end - identical and equal to the dispatch digest. Predecessor v8 and both v8 verdict files re-measured and matching, including my own at 50c9c59a..., confirming the bytes folded are the bytes I filed. v9 parses under a duplicate-key-rejecting pairs hook with 0 duplicate keys.
whatIVerified.repairLogVsActualDiff: 20 diff sites, 20 named. repairLog[0:55] byte-identical to v8's complete log. Method roster matches the appended entries as a set.
whatIVerified.citationsReMeasured: All four digests newly cited in whatThisDoesNotDo[1] were re-measured against live bytes, and both v1 review files were opened to confirm their verdict fields read REJECT. Corpus v2's header was read from its own bytes to test the reviewStatus and lineage claims.
whatIVerified.sourcePins: Every binding source re-measured. SRC-08, SRC-D and SRC-FRZ live digests are unchanged from reMeasurementAtV8's record; SRC-02 and SRC-03 still match their v2 pins. The whole /sources subtree is byte-identical to v8.
whatIVerified.carriedContent: manifestSchema, indexSchema, lockSchema, rejectionRules, testCorpusRequirements, identityDependencies, namedDifferencesFromPrototype, measuredPrototypeBaselines and sources all verified byte-identical to v8 as whole subtrees.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not re-review v2 through v8 on their merits beyond confirming repairLog[0:55] is byte-identical and the named invariants are unchanged as whole subtrees.

I did not review either fixture-corpus candidate's contents. I measured digests, read the verdict field of v1's two independent reviews, and read v2's header fields, solely to test v9's empirical claims. I express no view here on either candidate's quality or standing.
I did not evaluate DR-111's constraint or compatibility semantics, DR-112's ceremony, or the canonical-JSON profile. I confirmed only that v9 leaves them deferred exactly as v8 did.
I did not verify each named property of the moved SRC-08 / SRC-D / SRC-FRZ documents against their v2 bytes; I verified the live digests match the record carried at reMeasurementAtV8.
I did not read the other current v9 reviewer's file.
I did not assess DR-103's register status and express no view on it. I did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md; advisory V9-A3 reports a register-side obligation without acting on it.

I could not establish the exact authoring order of v9 and the corpus-v2 edit from bytes alone. I inferred it from corpus v2 pinning v9's digest, which requires v9 to exist first, and I state that inference as an inference in V9-S1.
This verdict is about the artifact's internal consistency and its handling of both v8 verdicts. It is not a statement that DR-103's acceptance-evidence cell is discharged.
